network.remove_publisher_confirm: Remove this publisher and all its routes from this phone? You can re-import the file later.
network.family.unsupported.help: This build of Daal cannot dial this transport. Routes of this kind will not connect.
network.family.experimental.help: Experimental transport — unproven in the field. It may fail to connect.
network.family.tuic.help: TUIC: a second QUIC route, and it is here for variety rather than as a way through. It runs over UDP on port 8443, and on Iranian networks that allow only ports 53, 80 and 443 both of those are shut — the same wall Hysteria2 runs into. It helps on networks where UDP still works and one QUIC route is already being watched. Where the others are blocked, this is not a new way in.
network.family.wireguard.help: WireGuard: fast and widely used, and one of the first shapes Iranian operators block on sight — it runs over UDP and its handshake is easy to recognise. AmneziaWG, the disguised version, does hold up there; this build cannot produce that disguise, so an AmneziaWG configuration is imported as ordinary WireGuard and loses it. Worth having where WireGuard is allowed. Do not count on it where it is not.
network.family.amneziawg.help: AmneziaWG: a route labelled AmneziaWG cannot be dialled at all — this build's engine has no AmneziaWG support, so its disguise settings cannot be applied. Separately, an AmneziaWG configuration you paste is imported as an ordinary WireGuard route: that one connects where WireGuard is allowed, but not where WireGuard is blocked, which is the whole reason AmneziaWG exists.
network.family.anytls.help: Looks like ordinary web traffic and pads the size of what it sends inside the protocol itself, so how much you send and when is harder to recognise. It also reuses one connection for many requests instead of opening a fresh one each time. It listens on an unusual port, so it will not work on networks that allow only ports 53, 80 and 443.
network.family.shadowsocks.help: Shadowsocks: the one transport here that does not start with a TLS handshake, so it stays reachable when the TLS-based routes are being detected together. It is not a stronger route — Shadowsocks is the kind censors have studied the longest, and on its own it is one of the easier ones to spot. It listens on an unusual port, so it will not work on networks that allow only ports 53, 80 and 443. It is here so that not everything fails at once.
network.family.tor_bridge.help: Reaches the internet through the Tor network using a bridge — a relay whose address is not published. Works without any Daal server of your own. This build of Daal does not include the Tor software itself, so bridge routes cannot connect yet.
import.tor_bridge.title: Add Tor bridges

settings.custody.rotate.dialog.title: Rotate your Daal address?

settings.custody.rotate.dialog.checkbox: I understand publishers must learn my new address.

pub.recipients.title: Recipients
pub.recipients.empty.title: No recipients yet
pub.recipients.empty.help: Add a friend's daal1… address to start distributing routes.
pub.recipients.revoke.title: Revoke recipient?
pub.recipients.revoke.body: Revoke {name}? They lose access on the next freshness rotation.
pub.recipients.remove.title: Remove from list?
pub.recipients.remove.body: Remove {name} from your roster for good? This only clears the local record — it was already revoked on the server.
pub.recipients.rotate.title: Give {name} a new key?
pub.recipients.rotate.body: The relay will issue {name} a fresh key and cancel the one they have now. The file they are using stops working the moment this finishes, so you will have to send them the new one. Nobody else needs a new file — everyone else keeps connecting with the one they already have, though every connection on this relay briefly drops and comes back.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.title: {name} has a new key
pub.recipients.rotate.done.body: The old key is cancelled. Until {name} imports the new file they cannot connect, and Daal has no way to send it to them over the network — hand it to them yourself. Everyone else on this relay was left alone.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.box_keys: The relay did more than it was asked: it replaced its own identity as well, so EVERY file you have handed out has stopped working — not only {name}'s. Rebuild each one in the files list above and deliver them all again.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.unverified: The relay would not say which parts of itself it rewrote, so nothing confirmed the old key is gone everywhere. Treat the old file as possibly still working until this relay's management service is updated.
pub.recipients.rotate.done.nofile: The key was changed on the relay, but the new file could not be built. {name} is disconnected until you rebuild it — use Rebuild in the files list above.
pub.recipients.add.title: Add recipient
pub.recipients.add.bad_address: That doesn't look like a daal1… address.
pub.relays.title: Relays
pub.relays.destroy.title: Remove {name}?
pub.relays.destroy.intro: Two very different things go by that word. Pick the one you mean.
pub.relays.destroy.local.title: Remove from Daal only
pub.relays.destroy.local.body: Erases this relay’s signing key and cloud token from this app and drops it from your list. The server itself keeps running and keeps billing, and connection files you have already handed out keep working. Write the address down now — afterwards Daal can no longer show it to you, and your provider’s console is the only place left to delete it.
pub.relays.destroy.address.unknown: Daal has no address for this server.
pub.relays.destroy.server.title: Delete the server too
pub.relays.destroy.server.body: Destroys the cloud server itself, along with the SSH key and firewall Daal created for it. Everyone using this relay loses their connection the moment it goes, billing stops, and none of it can be undone or recovered.
pub.relays.destroy.server.noaddr: Daal never recorded an address for this relay, so it will look the server up by the name it gave it. If it cannot find it, the report will say so and you will have to finish the job in your provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.error.local: Nothing was removed. The relay is still in Daal — try again.
pub.relays.destroy.error.server: The server was NOT deleted, and nothing was removed from Daal. It is still running and still billing — try again, or delete it yourself in your cloud provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.title: What happened
pub.relays.destroy.report.ok: The server is gone and the billing has stopped. Anyone who was using this relay is disconnected now.
pub.relays.destroy.report.local_only: Removed from Daal. The server is still running and still billing — delete it in your cloud provider’s console to stop the charges.
pub.relays.destroy.report.server_failed: The server was NOT deleted. It is still running and still billing, and Daal can no longer reach it — delete it yourself in your cloud provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.leftovers: The server is gone, but Daal could not clear everything it had created alongside it. The leftovers cost nothing, but they can block a new relay in the same region — remove them in your provider’s console.
pub.relays.destroy.report.local_kept: The relay is still in Daal. Nothing on this device was erased, so you can try again once the problem above is sorted out.
pub.relays.status.disclaimer: Setup state — not a live health check.
pub.relays.empty.title: No relays yet
pub.relays.empty.body: A relay is your own small server. You create one, then hand out a connection file to the people you want to share it with.
pub.artifacts.title: Files to share
pub.artifacts.shared.title: Everyone pack (.sbp)
pub.artifacts.shared.missing.title: No everyone pack yet
pub.artifacts.shared.missing.body: This is the one file anyone in your family can import on any phone. Build it once and share it as often as you like.
pub.artifacts.rotate.title: Rotate the everyone pack?
pub.artifacts.rotate.body: This mints new shared credentials. Every copy of the pack you have already handed out will stop working and everyone will need the new file. Use it if the old one leaked; use plain Share otherwise.
pub.artifacts.raw.title: Raw signed bundle (.sbp)
pub.artifacts.sbpx.missing: This recipient's file was never written. Rebuild it to try again.
pub.artifacts.copied: Copied. Paste it into a chat message — the whole block, including every line.
qr.send.title: Show this to their phone
qr.send.what: This is the everyone pack for {relay}, travelling as light instead of as a file. It goes straight from this screen to their camera — no network is involved at any point.
qr.send.how: Hold the two phones about a hand's width apart, screen facing camera. Open the QR import on their phone and point it here. Keep both hands steady: the code changes several times a second and their phone collects the pieces until it has the whole file.
qr.send.state.usual: Most phones have enough by about now — keep going until theirs says so.
qr.send.state.enough: A whole copy has been shown. If their phone has not finished, keep going: nothing is wasted, the pieces keep adding up.
qr.send.speed.label: If their camera is struggling
qr.send.canvas.alt: Animated QR code carrying the connection file
qr.send.error.title: The code stopped
qr.send.error.body: Nothing was sent. If the everyone pack has not been built yet, close this and build it first — that is the file this sends.
pub.recipients.adding_detail: Opening a 5-minute window on the server firewall, minting credentials, and registering the recipient. Stay on this screen — typically 10–30 seconds.
pub.recipients.err_unreachable: The server isn't answering on its management port. If it was created with an older build of Daal it can't be patched in place — remove it from Daal in the danger zone below, delete the server in your provider's console, and deploy a fresh one.
pub.helper_ip.title: Your network address changed
pub.helper_ip.body: Daal opens a short-lived opening in the server's firewall for the address you're connecting from. We couldn't work it out automatically — check the address below and try again.
pub.helper_ip.stale: Couldn't reach the relay from this network.
pub.danger.title: Danger zone
pub.danger.recovery.title: Save a recovery key
pub.danger.recovery.body: This relay's signing key lives on this device only. If you lose the device you can never add or remove anyone again. Save a copy somewhere safe — but read the warning first: the file is NOT encrypted.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.title: Change this relay's disguise
pub.danger.rotate_tls.body: The relay disguises itself as an ordinary web server at one hostname. If that hostname has been singled out and blocked, changing it can bring the relay back — at the cost of every connection file you have handed out.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.title: Change the disguise on {relay}?
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.body: Every connection file you have handed out stops working the moment this finishes — the everyone pack and each person's own file alike. The files people are holding carry no refresh address, so nothing can tell them: you have to rebuild each file on this screen and deliver it by hand, one person at a time. Nobody's key changes and the relay keeps running; only the disguise moves.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.count: {count} people are holding a file that will stop working.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.count_none: Nobody is holding a file from this relay yet, so right now this costs you nothing.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.count: {count} people are holding a file that has stopped working.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.count_none: Nobody was holding a file from this relay, so this cost you nothing.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.title: Disguise changed
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.next: Every file you have handed out is dead. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file in the list above, then deliver each one by hand — the files they are holding carry no refresh address, so nothing can reach them over the network.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.unknown: The relay would not confirm which hostname it landed on, so the name above is the one that was asked for, not one that was checked. The files Daal builds will use it — if people still cannot connect after importing them, this relay's management service needs updating.
pub.rotate.too_old: This relay's management service is older than this app and cannot do that on its own, so nothing was changed. That service is fixed when the relay is created and cannot be patched in place — it needs a new release of Daal, or a fresh relay.
pub.danger.decommission.title: Remove this relay
pub.danger.decommission.body: Take it out of Daal and leave the server running, or delete the server as well and stop the billing. You pick which on the next screen.
pub.custody.label.hardware: Protected by this device's secure hardware. The key cannot be copied off this device.
pub.custody.label.os_keystore: Protected by this device's system keystore — software only, with no dedicated secure hardware.
pub.custody.label.session_passphrase: Protected by a session passphrase you type once each time Daal starts. This device has no keystore Daal can use, so the protection is only as strong as your passphrase.
pub.custody.broken.title: Can't reach this device's key store
pub.custody.broken.body: Daal can't open the place where this relay's signing key is kept, so every publisher action would fail halfway. Nothing has been lost. Restart the app; if it keeps happening, export a recovery key while you still can.
pub.custody.recovery.help: Export a recovery key while one is still readable:
pub.custody.migrate.title: One-time security upgrade
pub.custody.migrate.body: Daal no longer uses a PIN. Your relay's keys move into this device's own protected storage and you'll never be asked for the PIN again. Enter it once to complete the move.
pub.custody.migrate.warn: Don't skip this. If you do, the signing key for {n} relay(s) becomes permanently unreadable — you could never add or remove anyone on them again.
pub.custody.migrate.done: Done. Your keys are protected by this device now, and the PIN is gone for good.
pub.custody.migrate.partial: Some items couldn't be moved. Your old copies are untouched — nothing has been lost.
pub.custody.unlock.title: Unlock your publisher keys
pub.custody.unlock.body: This device has no keystore Daal can use, so your keys are protected by a session passphrase. Enter it once per launch.
pub.danger.recovery.confirm:
Save an unencrypted recovery key?

The file contains this relay’s signing key in the clear. It goes to your Downloads folder, where any app with storage access can read it, and Daal’s emergency wipe cannot remove it. Anyone who gets this file can impersonate your relay.

Move it to secure storage and delete it from Downloads as soon as you have.
pub.custody.recovery.confirm:
Save an unencrypted recovery key?

The file contains this relay’s signing key in the clear. It goes to your Downloads folder, where any app with storage access can read it, and Daal’s emergency wipe cannot remove it. Anyone who gets this file can impersonate your relay.

Move it to secure storage and delete it from Downloads as soon as you have.
pub.artifacts.sbpx.revoked: Revoked. Their file no longer works and cannot be rebuilt — add them again if you want to give them access.
pub.artifacts.shared.build.title: Build the everyone pack?
pub.artifacts.shared.build.body: Building mints fresh shared credentials on the relay. If you have already handed out an everyone pack for this relay — even though the file is missing from this device — those copies will stop working and everyone will need the new file.
pub.custody.unlock.create.title: Choose a passphrase
pub.custody.unlock.create.body: This device has no keystore Daal can use, so your publisher keys are protected by a passphrase you choose now and type once each time Daal starts. It is never stored and cannot be recovered — if you forget it, the relay’s signing key is gone and you could never add or remove anyone on it again. Type it twice.
pub.custody.unlock.create.mismatch: Those don't match. Type the same passphrase twice.
pub.custody.unlock.regression: If you have never set a passphrase on this device, nothing is lost: your system keystore has stopped answering. Unlock your login keyring (or restart the device) and reopen Daal.
pub.custody.migrate.stuck.body: The PIN was never stored anywhere, so there is no way to recover it and no way to read the old key without it. The only way forward is to remove the affected relay from Daal and start a new one. Its server keeps running and billing until you delete it in your provider’s console.
pub.custody.migrate.stuck.confirm:
Remove {name} from Daal?

Its signing key is unreadable without the PIN, so this is permanent: you will never be able to add or remove anyone on that relay again. The server at {ip} keeps running and keeps billing — delete it in your cloud provider’s console.
pub.fresh.title: Refresh addresses
pub.fresh.pack.healing: The files people are holding can repair themselves
pub.fresh.pack.healing.body: They carry {count} refresh addresses. When you change something about this relay, each person's app finds the new settings on its own — once it is not connected, because Daal will not fetch new settings through the tunnel it is trying to repair.
pub.fresh.pack.not_healing: The files people are holding cannot repair themselves
pub.fresh.pack.not_healing.body: Nothing you set up here changes a file somebody already has. Add two refresh addresses below, then rebuild the files and hand them out once more. After that, changes to this relay fix themselves.
pub.fresh.pack.not_healing.body_dated: Anything you handed out before {date} has no refresh address in it and never will. Add two addresses below, then rebuild the files and hand them out once more — after that, changes to this relay fix themselves.
pub.fresh.none.title: No refresh addresses yet
pub.fresh.none.body: A refresh address is a place on the ordinary web where Daal leaves a small signed note saying “the file changed, get the new one here”. You need two, at two different companies, before Daal will put them into a file.
pub.fresh.single.title: One address is not enough, and Daal will not use it
pub.fresh.single.body: The address sits inside every file you hand out: short, unique, and easy to watch for. Whoever can block your relay can block one hosting company just as easily — and then nothing repairs itself while you believe it does. Add a second one at a different company.
pub.fresh.pack_url.title: Where the rebuilt file will be downloadable
pub.fresh.pack_url.body: The note only says “the file changed, get it here”. Put the web address the rebuilt file will sit at — the same address every time. It must start with https.
pub.fresh.no_credential: The key for this address is missing from this device, so nothing can be published here.
pub.fresh.publish.title: Publish the note now
pub.fresh.publish.body: Signs a fresh note for the pack as it stands and uploads that note to every address. It does NOT upload the pack itself — put the rebuilt file at the download address above yourself, or the note will point at a file that is not there. Do this after you rebuild the files, and any time a publish has failed.
pub.fresh.blocked.title: Nothing was published
pub.fresh.blocked.no_signed_pack: This relay has no signed file yet. Build one first — there is nothing for the note to point at.
pub.fresh.blocked.no_pack_url: Fill in where the rebuilt file will be downloadable. The note has nowhere to point until you do.
pub.fresh.blocked.too_few_providers: Add a second refresh address at a different company. Daal will not publish to only one.
pub.fresh.result.degraded: The note did not reach enough places
pub.fresh.result.count: {ok} of {total} accepted it; {min} are required. Anyone who can only reach a refused one will not hear about a change.
pub.fresh.add.title: Add a refresh address
pub.fresh.add.body: Daal uploads a small signed note here every time this relay changes. Pick a company you already have an account with, and if you can, a place that already serves other traffic.
pub.fresh.add.credential_note: The key you paste can replace the note every one of your recipients trusts. It is kept on this device the same way your signing key is: never written into a file you share, a log, or a report, and never shown again after this.
pub.fresh.remove.confirm:
Remove this refresh address?

The key stored for it is deleted from this device as well. Files you have already handed out still name this address and will keep trying it.
pub.fresh.privacy.title: What this costs you
pub.fresh.privacy.body: Everyone holding a file checks these same addresses on a schedule. Whoever can read that company's logs can count your readers and see roughly where they are. And because Daal refuses to fetch new settings through the tunnel it is trying to repair, the check goes over the plain network where the local internet provider can see it — which is also the only reason it still works when the tunnel is already dead. Pointing these at a place that already serves other traffic makes the check look like ordinary browsing.
pub.danger.address.title: Change this relay's address
pub.danger.address.body: The relay answers on one internet address. If that address has been blocked, moving to another one brings the relay back in seconds — the server keeps running and nobody's key changes.
pub.danger.address.unavailable: Your hosting company cannot reserve a movable address from inside Daal, so there is nothing to move here. Reserve one in your hosting company's control panel and attach it to this server, then come back. Until then, the only way to change this relay's address is to rebuild it.
pub.danger.address.confirm.title: Change the address of {relay}?
pub.danger.address.confirm.body: The server keeps running, nobody's key changes, and nobody has to be re-added. Only the address people connect to moves, and it takes a few seconds.
pub.danger.address.confirm.self_heal: The files people are holding carry refresh addresses, so their apps will find the new address on their own. Not instantly: Daal will not fetch new settings through the tunnel it is trying to repair, so anyone still connected on the old address follows only after that connection drops.
pub.danger.address.confirm.no_self_heal: The files people are holding have no refresh address, so nothing will tell them. Every one of those files stops working the moment this finishes, and you will have to rebuild each of them on this screen and deliver them by hand.
pub.danger.address.confirm.count: {count} people are holding a file that names the old address.
pub.danger.address.confirm.count_none: Nobody is holding a file from this relay yet, so right now this costs you nothing.
pub.danger.address.confirm.old_ip: The old address stops serving once Daal has released it, which happens at the end of this. If you have given it out anywhere else — a note, a chat, another app — that stops working too.
pub.danger.address.confirm.old_ip_primar: This relay is still on the address the server was born with, and your hosting company will not let anyone take that away — so it keeps answering after the move. Changing the address gives people a second way in; it does not close the first. If you are doing this because the current address was blocked, that block stays exactly where it is.
pub.danger.address.field.fip_help: Leave this empty and Daal reserves a new address for this relay at your hosting company, in the same location. Fill it in only if you already reserved one yourself — then it is that address's ID number in your hosting company's control panel, not the address itself.
pub.danger.address.field.fip_help_manual: The reserved address's ID at your hosting company — the number on that address's page, not the address itself. You have to reserve it there first; Daal cannot reserve one on this hosting company.
pub.danger.address.field.fip_same: That is the address this relay is already on. Re-attaching it would change nothing, so the relay would stay blocked. Leave the field empty for a new one, or enter a different ID.
pub.danger.address.done.title: Address changed
pub.danger.address.done.body: The relay now answers on the new address. The old one no longer serves.
pub.danger.address.done.body_kept: The relay now answers on the new address. The old address ({ip}) is the server's own, so it cannot be released — it is still answering, and anyone who has it can still reach this relay.
pub.danger.address.done.self_heal: A fresh note has been published. One thing is still yours to do: the note only says “the file changed, get it here”, so put the rebuilt file at the address you set under Refresh addresses — Daal signs and publishes the note, but it never uploads the file itself. Once the file is there, the apps holding an old one pick up the new address on their own, whenever they are not connected.
pub.danger.address.done.no_self_heal: Every file you have handed out is dead. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file in the list above, then deliver each one by hand.
pub.danger.advice.title: What should you change?
pub.danger.advice.body: Daal can read what this computer has recorded while connecting and say which of the changes below fits it — or say plainly that it cannot tell. It never makes the change; you do.
pub.danger.advice.unknown.title: Daal cannot tell you what to change.
pub.danger.advice.destroys: This one destroys the server and builds a new one. New address, new keys, and every file you have ever handed out stops working until each person gets a new one. If the rebuild fails partway you can be left paying for two servers.
pub.danger.advice.unverified: Daal has not asked this relay whether it can do this, so it may refuse. Nothing is lost if it does — it refuses before it changes anything.
pub.danger.advice.saw_nothing: What it saw: nothing. No connection to this relay has failed on this computer inside the last two hours.
pub.danger.advice.unrecognised: Seen, but not something changing the relay would fix: {list}
pub.danger.advice.absent.title: What Daal could not see:
pub.danger.advice.scope: This is what THIS computer observed while connecting — not a survey of the relay, and not what the people you gave files to are seeing. If someone in the field is being blocked, that only reaches you if they send you their diagnostics.
pub.danger.advice.advice_only: This is advice only. Nothing here changes anything — use the buttons below when you have decided.
pub.danger.advice.level.l1: new keys for one person (below, on their row)
pub.danger.advice.level.l6: rebuild with a different mix of connection types
pub.danger.rotate_tls.confirm.body_fresh: Every connection file you have handed out stops working the moment this finishes — the everyone pack and each person's own file alike. But the files people hold do carry refresh addresses, so this one is repairable without a courier: rebuild the files on this screen, put the rebuilt everyone pack at the address you set under Refresh addresses, then press Publish there. Their apps pick the new settings up on their own after that. Nobody's key changes and the relay keeps running; only the disguise moves.
pub.danger.rotate_tls.done.next_fresh: Everything you have handed out is dead until you rebuild it. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file above, put the rebuilt everyone pack at the address you set under Refresh addresses — Daal publishes the note, never the file — then press Publish there. After that their apps find the new settings by themselves and you do not have to deliver anything.
scan.title: Scan a route
scan.lede: Point your camera at the moving code on the other screen. The code repeats itself, so hold steady until every block has arrived.
scan.discard.confirm: Discard the blocks decoded so far?
scan.progress.paused: Paused. Nothing decoded so far has been lost — resume when you are ready.
scan.stall.title: The scan has stopped making progress
scan.stall.body: {n} blocks are still missing. The other screen may have dimmed, or the camera may have lost focus. Keep the whole code inside the frame — it repeats, so the missing blocks come around again.
scan.stall.nothing: No frame has decoded yet. Check that the whole code is inside the frame and that the other screen is bright.
scan.cam.requesting: Asking for permission to use the camera…
scan.cam.denied.title: Camera permission was refused
scan.cam.denied.body: Daal uses the camera only to read the code on the other screen. Nothing is recorded and nothing leaves this device.
scan.cam.blocked.title: The camera is blocked for Daal
scan.cam.blocked.body: This device will not ask again, so it has to be changed by hand: open Settings → Apps → Daal → Permissions → Camera and choose Allow, then come back and start the scan. If you would rather not turn the camera on at all, use Paste frames — it needs no permission.
scan.cam.none.title: No camera found
scan.cam.none.body: This device has no camera available.
scan.cam.busy.title: The camera is already in use
scan.cam.busy.body: Another app is holding the camera. Close it, then try again.
scan.cam.unavailable.title: The camera cannot be opened here
scan.cam.unavailable.body: This build has no camera access.
scan.paste.label: One frame per line — either the plain frame text, or the JSON lines that daal-deploy qr-fountain prints.
scan.paste.none: There are no usable frames in that text.
scan.paste.rejected: {n} line(s) were not readable frames and were skipped.
scan.err.title: The import failed
scan.incomplete.title: Not enough of the route arrived
scan.incomplete.body: {n} of {total} blocks are still missing, so there is nothing complete to import yet. Keep scanning, or feed more frames.
scan.contract.title: This build is inconsistent
scan.contract.body: The app and its engine disagree about the scan format, so a scan could not be trusted to finish. This is a bug in the build, not something you can fix here. Please report it.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.title: Move this relay to another datacentre
pub.danger.rebuild.region.body: Daal deletes this server and builds a new one somewhere else. It is the answer to a whole range of addresses being blocked at once — and it costs you everything you have handed out.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.unavailable: Daal has no list of datacentres for your hosting company, so it cannot offer you a safe choice here. Set up a new relay in the place you want instead, then take this one down once everyone has moved across.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.field: Where to build the new relay
pub.danger.rebuild.region.same_zone: {to} sits in the same part of the internet as {from}, so the new relay will have much the same neighbours. If a whole range was blocked, the new address may land inside it again. Somewhere further away is the stronger move.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.other_zone: {to} is in a different part of the internet from {from} — {zone_from} to {zone_to} — so the new relay gets genuinely different neighbours.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.checking: Asking your hosting company what {region} offers…
pub.danger.rebuild.region.type_missing: {region} does not offer this relay's size of server ({type}). The old server is deleted before the new one is built, so choosing this would leave you with no relay at all. Pick somewhere else.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.type_unknown: Daal could not ask your hosting company what {region} offers, so it cannot promise the new server can be built there. The old server is deleted first, so if the build fails you are left with no relay. Try again before you continue.
pub.danger.rebuild.region.type_ok: {region} can host this relay's size of server ({type}).
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.title: Change which ways in this relay offers
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.body: Daal deletes this server and builds a new one offering a different set of ways in. Use it when the way people connect is what is being caught, rather than where the relay is.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.drops: It will stop offering: {families}. Anyone whose app was using one of those falls back to the ones that remain.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.drops_udp: Those need UDP. Where UDP is throttled or blocked they were not carrying anything anyway, and a connection shaped like that is itself something worth noticing — which is the point of dropping them.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.no_change: This set would leave the relay offering exactly what it offers now. Daal can only take ways in away here, never add one back: the rebuild is handed the list this relay serves today and keeps whichever of those the new set also has. So this would delete the server, kill every file you have handed out, and leave behind a relay nothing can tell apart from this one. Pick a different set.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.never_adds: This can only take ways in away. It cannot give back one this relay has already stopped offering — for that, set up a new relay.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.anytls: This set switches AnyTLS on. A file that includes AnyTLS can only be opened by an app updated after AnyTLS was added — on an older app the whole file is refused, not just that one way in. Make sure everyone you hand a file to can update first.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.title: Rebuild {relay}?
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.destroys: The server is deleted and a new one is built in its place. The new relay has a different address and different keys, so every connection file you have ever handed out stops working.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.downtime: Nobody can connect for about {est} while this runs.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.half_way: The old server is deleted before the new one is built. If the second half fails you have no relay at all, and there is no way back to the old server — you would have to build this relay again from the start.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.count: {count} people are holding a file that will stop working.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.count_none: Nobody is holding a file from this relay yet, so right now this costs you nothing.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.by_hand: The files people are holding have no refresh address, so nothing can tell them. You have to rebuild every file on this screen and deliver each one by hand, person by person.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.by_hand_fresh: The files people are holding do carry refresh addresses, so this one is repairable without a courier: rebuild the files on this screen, put the rebuilt everyone pack at the address you set under Refresh addresses, then press Publish there. Their apps pick the new relay up on their own after that, whenever they are not connected.
pub.danger.rebuild.confirm.no_undo: There is no undo. Daal's “go back to the previous file” only picks an older file out of this relay's history, and after this that file names a server that no longer exists.
pub.danger.rebuild.type_name: Type this relay's name to confirm:
pub.danger.rebuild.type_name_wrong: That is not this relay's name. Nothing has happened yet.
pub.danger.rebuild.done.title: Relay rebuilt
pub.danger.rebuild.done.body: The new relay is up and Daal has re-signed its connection file. It answers on a new address, with new keys.
pub.danger.rebuild.done.by_hand: Every file you have handed out is dead. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file in the list above, then deliver each one by hand.
pub.danger.rebuild.done.by_hand_fresh: Everything you have handed out is dead until you rebuild it. Rebuild the everyone pack and each person's file above, put the rebuilt everyone pack at the address you set under Refresh addresses — Daal publishes the note, never the file — then press Publish there.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.title: Move this relay to another hosting company
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.body: Daal deletes this server and builds a new one at a different company, on an account you pay for separately. It is the answer to your hosting company itself being the problem — its whole range blocked, or your account suspended — and it costs you everything you have handed out.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.unavailable: This copy of Daal can only build relays at the company this relay is already with, so there is nowhere to move it to. Set up a new relay elsewhere by hand instead, then take this one down once everyone has moved across.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.field: The company to build the new relay at
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.where.hetzne: A German company. Daal has built and run relays here.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.where.vultr: An American company. Daal can build relays here, but no relay has yet been run at Vultr — you would be the first.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.jurisdiction: The relay would sit under German and European law, and can be taken down on a complaint with notice. Hetzner cannot be paid for from inside Iran.

The relay would sit under United States law, and can be taken down on a complaint with notice. Vultr cannot be paid for from inside Iran. Nobody has yet checked whether Vultr's addresses are reachable from inside Iran — moving there might not fix what you are moving away from.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.field_token: The access key for your account at that company
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.token_help: Daal needs a key for the new company because the old key can only touch the old company. It is used to check the account and then to build the relay. Daal only keeps it once the new relay is actually running — if you close this, it is forgotten.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.field_region: Where to build the new relay
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.checking: Checking the account and asking what it offers…
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.field_type: The size of server to build
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.type_detail: {cpus} CPU · {memory} GB memory · {disk} GB disk · about {price} a month
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.type_none: That account offers no servers in that location. Pick somewhere else, or check the key is right.
pub.danger.rebuild.provider.two_bills: You will be paying {from} and {to} at the same time until you close the old account yourself. Daal deletes the old server, but it cannot close your account — and if you had reserved a movable address at {from}, it stays reserved and keeps costing you there.
pub.danger.rebuild.profile.no_families: This set has none of the ways in this relay currently offers, so the new relay would have no way in at all. Daal deletes the old server before it builds the new one, so choosing this would leave you with no relay. Pick a different set.
pub.danger.gone.title: This relay no longer exists
pub.danger.gone.body: A rebuild deleted this relay's server and could not build the replacement. The old server is gone and there is no way back to it. Every action below is against a machine that is not there any more.
pub.danger.gone.next: The way forward is to set up a new relay from the start. Once it is running, rebuild everyone's connection file and deliver each one, then remove this entry.
pub.danger.gone.audit_why: Before you build again: a build that fails part-way can leave a server still running and still costing you, and can leave a key behind that makes the next attempt fail. Daal can look at your account and tell you what is there. It only looks — it never removes anything.
pub.danger.gone.check: See what is left on my account
pub.danger.gone.found: Daal found these on your account:
pub.danger.gone.billing: This one keeps costing you money for as long as it stays on your account.
pub.danger.gone.nothing: Nothing of Daal's is left on your account. Nothing is billing you and nothing will block the next build.
pub.danger.gone.nothing_unproven: Daal found nothing of its own, but it could not read your full list of servers, so it cannot promise the account is clean. Check in your hosting company's control panel before you build again.
pub.danger.gone.incomplete: Daal could not read your full list of servers, so it cannot tell which of these is still in use and which is left over. Treat every line below as unproven and check it in your hosting company's control panel before removing anything.
pub.danger.advice.absent.no_failures: Nobody has reported a recognised failure on this relay recently, so there is no specific failure to move away from.
pub.danger.advice.absent.no_cooldown_pro: Nothing in Daal yet records that a whole address range, hosting company or network is in trouble. That is a gap in what Daal measures, not a sign that those are fine — so the steps that would answer such a problem can never be suggested from measurements.
pub.danger.advice.absent.no_prober: Daal does not yet test the network itself, so it has no first-hand readings of what is being blocked. Silence here means nothing was measured — not that everything was measured and looked fine.
pub.danger.advice.absent.operator_suppli: This answer is based on what you told Daal, not on a report from one of your recipients' own apps. That is why it cannot be more than moderately confident.
pub.danger.advice.reason.credential_leak: You told Daal that this relay's credentials may have leaked. Handing out new credentials answers that, and it does not touch the server.
pub.danger.advice.reason.no_cdn_candidat: This relay was set up to be reached through a CDN, and this version of Daal cannot build that. Changing the address is the cheapest change that exists today.
pub.danger.advice.reason.provider_suspen: The hosting company's account looks suspended or unreachable, so nothing on this server can be put right in place. Rebuilding at another hosting company is the way out.
pub.danger.advice.reason.udp_collapsed: UDP has stopped working on the network the person is connecting from. A relay built to use only TCP would get through.
pub.danger.advice.reason.protocol_famili: More than one kind of connection is failing at once, so this is not one blocked address or one blocked name. A different mix of connection types is what is left.
pub.danger.advice.reason.shared_risk_coo: The trouble is recorded against the whole network or hosting company this relay sits in, not against its own address. Moving to another datacentre leaves that range behind.
pub.danger.advice.reason.address_reset_a: Connections to this relay are being cut, and that was recorded against this relay's own address. Changing the address answers it, and the server, its keys and everyone's credentials are left alone.
pub.danger.advice.reason.address_reset_u: Connections to this relay are being cut. Nothing pinned that on this relay's address specifically — Daal cannot record that yet — but changing the address is the cheapest thing that would fix it, and it leaves the server, its keys and everyone's credentials alone.
pub.danger.advice.reason.address_timeout: Connections to this relay never complete, and that was recorded against this relay's own address. A server that is simply switched off looks exactly the same from here, so check the server is running before you change anything.

Connections to this relay never complete. That is weaker evidence than being cut off — a server that is simply switched off looks the same — and nothing pinned it on this relay's address. Check the server is running before you change anything.
pub.danger.advice.reason.address_block_n: The address is being blocked, and this relay cannot be given a new one ({detail}). Rebuilding in another datacentre gets a new address, but it destroys this server.
pub.danger.advice.reason.sni_block: The block is on the name this relay shows, not on its address. Changing the disguise answers it, and the server survives.
pub.danger.advice.reason.credential_leak: A leaked-credential failure was recorded on this relay. New credentials answer that without touching the server.
pub.danger.advice.reason.no_evidence_at_: Nothing has been recorded about this relay on this computer — no failure, no blocked address, no reading of the network. There is nothing here to base a change on, and this is not a reason to change anything.
pub.danger.advice.reason.nothing_matched: What was recorded ({detail}) is not something changing the relay would fix. Changing it would move the relay and leave the real problem where it is. This is not a reason to change anything.
